statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail is 20%, inside the watch band and below the block threshold, while Stress at 57% is the elevated reading.
recommendation: Mapped policy state is WATCH on Tail 20%. The elevated component is Stress at 57%, carried by Treasury churn at multi-decade highs rather than by observed Nasdaq-100 trend persistence. The narrow danger window spans the 18:00Z Fed Hammack appearance through the 20:00Z weekly cash close; after that the CME weekly halt removes the tradeable path entirely.
headline: Opening gain fully retraced; bond churn rather than Nasdaq trend carries the risk
body: The Nasdaq-100 opened higher, reached 30,649.20 and handed the entire gain back within the first cash hour, trading 30,490.73 (+0.04%) against a 30,413.59 day low, with the S&P 500 flat at 7,704.31. VIX is 15.67 and unchanged on the day inside a 15.02-15.92 range. That completed retracement is the decisive structural observation: an early directional attempt met supply and reverted, which is the opposite of the shallow-pullback, repeated-extension pattern that defines pathological price paths. Tail therefore stays in the watch band at 20%. The elevated reading sits in Stress. The 10-year yield is 5.20%, up about four basis points on the day inside a 5.17-5.22 range and near multi-decade highs, the 5-year is 5.04%, and the long end sits at multi-decade extremes after the 30-year reached 5.44% on Thursday, its highest since 2004, with the 2-year at 4.897%, its highest since 2023. Crude is easing but from elevated absolute levels, WTI near $93.79 (-0.87%) and Brent near $105.93, on reported US-Iran negotiations over a phased end to the Middle East conflict including a Strait of Hormuz reopening. Today's releases were benign to mixed: August durable goods orders came in flat against a -0.4% forecast, and final September Michigan sentiment revised up to 48.1 from 47.8 while one-year inflation expectations stayed at 4.6%. Shared Finviz context, collected at 14:12Z with a partial status because its calendar and futures sections failed, shows latest-session semiconductor strength and mixed megacaps with split sector breadth; it is delayed, non-real-time context and is not used here as evidence of current Nasdaq-100 structure. Cross-asset signals conflict, with yields rising while crude eases and equities sit flat, which reduces directional conviction rather than establishing trend persistence. Dominant mode is mixed.

lookbackSummary: The trailing 24 hours held a narrow band: Tail between 17% and 24%, Stress between 54% and 59%, and Confidence between 85% and 88%, alternating between EA_ON and WATCH without ever approaching the block threshold. Dominant mode rotated through mixed, normal and two brief trend-up readings during the European morning. The 13:00Z slot has no published Claude assessment and is marked unavailable rather than filled in.
outlookSummary: The near-term path keeps Tail in the watch band, rising only to 22% across the 18:00Z Fed Hammack appearance and the power hour into the Friday close, which together define the narrow danger window. The distinguishing feature of this window is that the CME weekly halt arrives inside the 20:00Z hour: the remaining seventeen hourly slots are halted, untradeable time in which no mean-reversion failure can develop, so Tail falls into the 9-12% range while Confidence decays from 83% to 55% as the last live observation ages. Stress stays moderate through the weekend and drifts up slightly at the end to reflect accumulated weekend uncertainty from the unresolved US-Iran track and a bond market at multi-decade yield extremes, both of which reprice at the Sunday reopen outside this window rather than inside any hour of it.

forecast.analysis: Observed this hour: NDX pushed to 30,649 then handed the whole gain back, trading 30,490 (+0.04%) with SPX flat and the 30,413 day low already tested. VIX 15.67, unchanged. That completed retracement argues against one-way structure, while the 10Y at 5.20% (+4bp) keeps Stress elevated.
drivers: Opening gain fully retraced inside the first cash hour
10Y at 5.20%, +4bp, intraday range 5.17-5.22
VIX 15.67 and flat: no volatility expansion observed
WTI -0.87% to $93.79 on reported phased US-Iran deal

forecast.analysis: Second cash hour. Base case is continued two-way trade inside the 30,413-30,649 opening range established earlier. A decisive break of that range alongside a further yield push would be the first genuine amplifier; absent it, retracements are assumed to keep arriving.
drivers: Opening range 30,413-30,649 is the first structural checkpoint
Conditional: sustained 10Y break above 5.22% would amplify
Mid-morning liquidity usually absorbs the opening imbalance

forecast.analysis: The European cash close falls in this hour and typically withdraws a hedging bid, so a directional attempt can extend for a short stretch. Tail is nudged only for that liquidity transition; the working assumption stays that pullbacks still appear unless the opening range gives way.
drivers: European cash close removes a hedging bid
Bond churn at multi-decade highs stays the main Stress channel
No aligned amplifier stack observed as of the cutoff

forecast.analysis: Pre-speech hour before the 18:00Z Fed appearance, overlapping the start of Friday weekly-close positioning. The conditional risk is a rate-path repricing impulse transmitting into index futures. No such impulse is present at the assessment cutoff.
drivers: Fed Hammack scheduled 18:00Z as a rate-path checkpoint
Friday weekly-close positioning begins to build
Michigan 1y inflation expectations sticky at 4.6%

forecast.analysis: The scheduled Fed Hammack appearance lands in this hour. With the 30Y at 5.44%, its highest since 2004, and the 10Y around 2007 highs, hawkish rate-path language is the plausible trigger for a faster directional leg. Treated as a checkpoint, not an observed path.

30Y 5.44% highest since 2004; 2Y 4.897% highest since 2023

Conditional: a rates impulse would need to deny retracement

forecast.analysis: Power hour into the Friday close: the session's thinnest-conviction, highest-imbalance window. The conditional risk here is a one-way drift on weekly rebalancing rather than a headline shock, and it only matters if retracements stop arriving, which is not the case at the cutoff.
drivers: US power hour and weekly-close rebalancing imbalance
Weekly close lands with the long end near multi-decade highs
Conditional: failing retracements would raise Tail intraday

forecast.analysis: Cash close at 20:00Z and the CME weekly halt both fall in this hour, so the tradeable path collapses before it ends. Residual risk is confined to the closing auction; once the halt takes effect no mean-reversion failure can develop.
drivers: US cash close and CME weekly futures halt at 20:00Z
Closing auction is the last liquid imbalance of the week
After the halt there is no live price path to fail

forecast.analysis: First hour after the weekly futures halt. With no tradeable NQ path the pathological-path risk this hour is structurally near zero; the residual score reflects only that the last observed structure is now a closing print rather than live evidence.
drivers: Futures halted for the weekend from 20:00Z
Score reflects absence of a tradeable path, not calm markets
Last observed reference: NDX 30,490 area into the close

forecast.analysis: Friday evening with the halt in force. Attention shifts to whether weekend reporting changes the rates or Middle East picture; any repricing would express itself at the Sunday reopen, outside this 24-hour window rather than inside this hour.
drivers: Halt in force: no intra-hour price discovery possible
Weekend reporting risk accrues toward the Sunday reopen
US-Iran negotiations in New York remain unresolved

forecast.analysis: Late Friday in Europe, early evening in New York. Nothing scheduled and no market open, so this hour carries only headline-accumulation risk. Confidence steps down because the live price path behind it is now several hours old.
drivers: No scheduled macro release in this hour
Confidence decays as the last live observation ages
Oil direction hinges on the reported phased-deal talks

forecast.analysis: Saturday begins with every relevant venue closed. The assessment for this hour rests on carried-over environment only: yields near multi-decade highs and oil easing from elevated levels, with no mechanism for path failure while trading is halted.
drivers: Saturday: all relevant venues closed
Carried-over environment: 10Y ~5.20%, WTI ~$94, Brent ~$106
No path-failure mechanism available during the halt

forecast.analysis: Overnight Saturday. Reporting on the phased Hormuz talks describes trust over sequencing as the sticking point and puts the odds of agreement before the November midterms well below even, so a weekend breakthrough is possible but not the base case, and nothing prices in this hour.
drivers: Phased Hormuz talks: sequencing and trust remain unresolved
Reported odds of a pre-midterm deal are well below even
Any weekend development prices only at the Sunday reopen

news.title: US and Iran discuss phased deal to reopen Hormuz and end US blockade, sources say

forecast.analysis: Deep overnight hour on Saturday. Asian and European desks are shut, so even a material headline would meet no liquidity. Scores stay low for Tail and moderate for Stress, describing the environment rather than any observable structure.
drivers: Asian and European desks shut: no liquidity to absorb news
Scores describe environment, not observable structure
Treasury volatility remains the dominant Stress theme

forecast.analysis: Saturday pre-dawn in Europe. No change is expected from the prior hour because no information channel is active. The forecast holds the same low Tail rather than manufacturing variation that the evidence does not support.
drivers: No active information channel in this hour
Holding scores flat is the evidence-supported choice
Next genuine repricing point is the Sunday futures reopen

forecast.analysis: Saturday early morning. Confidence crosses into the medium-low band here because the newest live NQ observation behind this slot is now more than half a day old, which is the honest description of a weekend halt.
drivers: Confidence enters medium-low: last live NQ print >12h old
Weekend halt, not thin trading: nothing is quotable
Tail stays low because no price path can fail

forecast.analysis: Saturday morning in Europe. The week's structural story is unchanged in this hour: rate volatility rather than Nasdaq trend persistence carried the risk, and that distinction is what keeps Tail low while Stress stays moderate.
drivers: Rate volatility, not index trend, carried the week's risk
Tail low and Stress moderate is the coherent weekend pairing
No scheduled US macro release over the weekend

forecast.analysis: Mid Saturday morning. Any Middle East or rate-path reporting published during this hour would be assessed against the Sunday reopen rather than this slot, so it does not lift this hour's Tail on its own.
drivers: Weekend reporting is assessed against the Sunday reopen
Headline existence alone does not lift this hour's Tail
Unresolved US-Iran track is the main weekend watch item

forecast.analysis: Saturday midday approaches with the halt unchanged. This hour is scored purely from the persistent backdrop: multi-decade-high long-end yields against an easing but still elevated crude complex, and a calm 15.67 VIX print from Friday.
drivers: Persistent backdrop: long-end yields at multi-decade highs
Crude easing from elevated levels, not from normal levels
Friday VIX close near 15.67 indicates no priced stress spike

forecast.analysis: Late Saturday morning. Friday's evidence still frames this hour, and its most useful feature was what did not happen: no shallow-pullback sequence and no repeated extension after a failed retracement, the two patterns that would have justified a higher Tail.
drivers: Friday showed no shallow-pullback or failed-retracement chain
Absence of those patterns is what keeps Tail in the low band
Halt unchanged: no new structure can form in this hour

forecast.analysis: Saturday midday. Nothing distinguishes this hour mechanically, so the assessment names the forward catalysts instead: the August core PCE print and the September employment report both fall inside the coming week and shape the next regime.
drivers: Core PCE (Aug) scheduled 2026-09-30 as the week's first test
September employment report scheduled 2026-10-02
Weekend halt still precludes any path failure this hour

forecast.analysis: Early Saturday afternoon. Tail ticks up by one only to mark that the window's remaining hours sit progressively closer to the Sunday reopen, where accumulated weekend information is repriced in a single gap. The reopen itself is outside this window.
drivers: Remaining hours sit progressively nearer the Sunday reopen
Accumulated weekend information reprices in one gap
Sunday reopen falls outside this 24-hour forecast window

forecast.analysis: Saturday afternoon. Stress edges up with the same reasoning: the longer the halt runs against an unresolved geopolitical negotiation and a churning bond market, the wider the plausible reopen distribution, even though this hour itself stays inert.
drivers: Longer halt against unresolved negotiation widens reopen range
Bond churn is the transmission channel to watch at the reopen
This hour itself remains inert with no tradeable path

forecast.analysis: Late Saturday afternoon in Europe. The scores continue their measured drift to reflect accumulated weekend uncertainty rather than any observation. Confidence is at its lowest in the window because the evidence base has not been refreshed since Friday's close.
drivers: Drift reflects accumulated uncertainty, not new observation
Confidence at window low: evidence unrefreshed since Friday

forecast.analysis: Final hour of the window, late Saturday. It carries the largest weekend-uncertainty allowance while remaining a halted, untradeable hour. Anything about the actual reopen path is explicitly beyond this forecast and belongs to a later assessment.
drivers: Largest weekend-uncertainty allowance in the window
